extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing use of certificates of correction (35 U.S.C. 255, 37 CFR 1.323/1.324) and petitions (37 CFR 1.78) to add/correct benefit claims, and rules for statutory/terminal disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement re: claims with effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not required to provide a statement if either (i) The application claims the benefit of a nonprovisional application in which a statement under § 1.55(k), paragraph (a)(6) of this section, or this paragraph that the application contains, or contained at any time, a claim to a claimed invention that has an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013 has been filed; or (ii) the applicant reasonably believes on the basis of information already known to the individuals designated in § 1.56(c) that the later filed application does not, and did not at any time, contain a claim to a claimed invention that has an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording provides the two alternative bases for omission of the statement; implementers should verify which condition applies before omitting the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy and translation for certain international benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to an international application or international design application which designates but did not originate in the United States, the Office may require a certified copy of such application together with an English translation if filed in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants claiming such benefit should be prepared to provide certified copies and translations when the parent did not originate in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to accept unintentionally delayed benefit claim (general requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and paragraph (d)(2) is presented after the time period, a claim for benefit may be accepted if the reference was unintentionally delayed; a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim must be accompanied by: (1) the required reference unless previously submitted; (2) the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information if delay is in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must include the reference, fee, and an unintentional delay statement; expect possible requests for additional substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentably indistinct claims across multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant or assignee contain patentably indistinct claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required in the absence of good and sufficient reason for their retention during pendency in more than one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid maintaining identical/patentably indistinct claims in multiple pending applications unless they can justify retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentably indistinct claims in reexamination/patents naming different inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent or application under reexamination and at least one other application naming different inventors are owned by the same person and contain patentably indistinct claims, and there is no record statement indicating common ownership or assignment obligation on the effective filing date (or date of invention), the Office may require a statement whether the claimed inventions were commonly owned or subject to assignment to the same person on such date, and if not, indicate which named inventor is the prior inventor. Even if commonly owned, patentably indistinct claims may be rejected under the doctrine of double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventorship differs, provide clear record evidence of common ownership/assignment or identify prior inventor to avoid double patenting issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of reference presentation requirement for pre-September 16, 2012 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before September 16, 2012 (or international applications under 35 U.S.C. 363 before that date), presenting the specific reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title satisfies the requirement to present a specific reference in an application data sheet (§ 1.76). This does not apply to references submitted for petitions under paragraph (b) to restore the benefit of a provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical filing-date cases may rely on specification-first-sentence references; confirm applicability by filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petitions for international applications not originally filed with USRO
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under paragraph (b), (c), or (e) is required in an international application that was not filed with the United States Receiving Office and is not a nonprovisional application, such petition may be filed in the earliest nonprovisional application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to the international application and will be treated as having been filed in the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits filing required petitions later in the earliest subsequent nonprovisional claiming benefit to the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 386(c) effective-date limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 386(c) with respect to an international design application is applicable only to nonprovisional applications, international applications, and international design applications filed on or after May 13, 2015, and patents issuing thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect 386(c) benefit for filings before May 13, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods in the section are non-extendable but subject to certain rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods set forth in this section are not extendable, but are subject to 35 U.S.C. 21(b) (and § 1.7(a)), PCT Rule 80.5, and Hague Agreement Rule 4(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the section's deadlines cannot be extended, other statutory/regulatory provisions may apply; verify applicability of those rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLTIA amendment effect on 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) and provisional benefit references
rubrics_metrics.description: PLTIA amended 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) to provide that no application shall be entitled to the benefit of an earlier-filed provisional unless an amendment containing the specific reference is submitted at such time during pendency as required by the Director; the Director may consider failure to submit within that time as a waiver and may establish procedures, including payment of fees, to accept unintentionally delayed submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director-level procedures may be promulgated; practitioners should watch USPTO guidance and fee rules for delayed provisional references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) change on certificates of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) is effective for all patents whenever granted and no longer requires that the amendment containing the specific reference be submitted during pendency. Thus, the prior prohibition on granting certificates of correction to add or correct a claim for the benefit of a prior provisional application no longer applies; a certificate of correction may now be available under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under current law, correcting/adding provisional benefit by certificate of correction is possible but still subject to the other conditions and limitations described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application special rule for submission of required reference
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3) was revised to make procedures under 37 CFR 1.78(e) to accept an unintentionally delayed benefit claim applicable to design applications; 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3)(i) provides the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) must be submitted during the pendency of the later-filed application. For design applications, this pendency period is the only applicable time period because the four-month/sixteen-month periods do not apply. If not submitted during pendency, a petition under 1.78(e) may be filed, and a petition under 1.78(e) may be filed along with a request for certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323 in a design patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applicants must submit required references during pendency or use 1.78(e) petition; combining petition and certificate request is permitted in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of errors correctable by certificate of correction for benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions a certificate of correction can be used, with respect to a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), to correct: (A) the failure to make reference to a prior copending nonprovisional/international application designating the U.S. or international design application designating the U.S. pursuant to 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2); (B) an incorrect reference to such prior applications pursuant to 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2); (C) the failure to make reference to a prior provisional application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3); or (D) an incorrect reference to a prior provisional application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates may correct specific types of missing/incorrect references to prior applications (both provisional and nonprovisional/international) when conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for certificate of correction for 35 U.S.C. 120 to a national application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a benefit claim based upon 35 U.S.C. 120 to a national application is to be asserted or corrected in a patent via a certificate of correction, the following conditions must be satisfied: (A) all requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(d)(1) must have been met in the application which became the patent; (B) it must be clear from the record of the patent and parent application(s) that priority is appropriate; and (C) a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.78(e) must be filed, including the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfy regulatory prerequisites and ensure the record shows entitlement to priority; prepare and file the grantable 1.78(e) petition with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for certificate of correction for international applications (35 U.S.C. 120 & 365(c)/386(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a benefit claim based upon 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) to an international application, or 35 U.S.C. 120 and 386(c) to an international design application, is to be asserted or corrected in a patent via a certificate of correction, the following conditions must be satisfied: (A) all requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(d)(1) must have been met in the application which became the patent; (B) it must be clear from the record that priority is appropriate; (C) the patentee must submit with the request copies of documentation showing designation of states and any other information needed to make clear from the record that 35 U.S.C. 120 priority is appropriate; and (D) a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e) must be filed including the petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International priority corrections require additional documentation showing state designations and a grantable 1.78(e) petition with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for certificate of correction for 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a benefit claim based upon 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a prior provisional application is to be asserted or corrected in a patent via a certificate of correction, the following conditions must be satisfied: (A) all requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(a)(1) and (a)(2) must have been met in the application which became the patent; (B) it must be clear from the record that priority is appropriate; and (C) a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.78(c) must be filed, including the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional-benefit corrections require compliance with the a(1)/a(2) regulatory prerequisites, proof of entitlement, and a grantable 1.78(c) petition with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate-of-correction not appropriate where further examination would be required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 is filed with a request for a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 in an issued patent, the petition should not be granted where grant would require further examination. Examples of further examination: (1) where grant would cause the patent to be subject to a different statutory framework (e.g., adding a benefit claim to a pre-March 16, 2013 filing causing FITF vs pre-AIA issues); (2) where grant would result in claims having a later effective filing date and thus more potential prior art; (3) where grant would alter the continuity chain requiring evaluation of continuity of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use certificates to effect changes that trigger substantive reexamination issues; consider reissue if further examination would be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate-of-correction should not be granted if it would appear to extend patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant of the petition under 37 CFR 1.78 with a request for a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 would have the appearance of extending the patent term, the petition should not be granted. Example: changing to a later filing date for the earliest application for which domestic benefit is claimed could appear to extend the patent term even if effective filing date doesn't change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid certificate grants that create the impression of patent-term extension; examine term consequences carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples where petition under 37 CFR 1.78 with certificate may be appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemplary appropriate situations include: (A) Adding or correcting a claim to a prior application having a filing date before March 16, 2013 to a patent examined under pre-AIA first-inventor-to-file provisions; (B) Adding/correcting a claim to a prior application before March 16, 2013 in a patent examined under AIA FITF when the 37 CFR 1.55/1.78 statement is filed concurrently; (C) Adding a claim to a prior application filed on or after March 16, 2013 in a patent examined under pre-AIA first-inventor provisions; (D) Adding/correcting a claim to a prior application filed on or after March 16, 2013 in a patent examined under AIA FITF provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples as guidance that context (filing dates and examination framework) can make certificates appropriate; ensure other conditions are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples where certificate under 35 U.S.C. 255 may not be appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemplary non-appropriate situations include: (A) Adding/correcting a claim to a prior application before March 16, 2013 in a patent examined under AIA FITF when the 37 CFR 1.55/1.78 statement is not present; (B) Correcting a claim from a prior application before March 16, 2013 to one on/after March 16, 2013 in a patent examined under pre-AIA law; (C) Correcting a claim to a prior application that would result in a later effective filing date for the claimed invention; (D) Correcting a claim that would have the appearance of extending the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examples align with a case at hand, certificates likely inappropriate; consider reissue or other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application when certificate conditions not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If the above-stated conditions are not satisfied or if the correction sought would require further examination, the filing of a reissue application may be appropriate to pursue the desired correction of the patent for benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c). Also, a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 cannot be used to remove a benefit claim because further examination would be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, or when further substantive changes are needed, pursue reissue rather than certificate of correction; certificates cannot remove benefit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing requests for certificates of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a certificate of correction should be addressed to: Commissioner for Patents, Office of Data Management Attention: Certificates of Correction Branch, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. A request filed via the USPTO electronic filing system should use the document description: Request for Certificate of Correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified address and electronic document description to ensure proper routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and recordation of requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for certificates of correction will be forwarded to the Certificates of Correction Branch where they will be listed in a permanent record book. If the patent is involved in an interference or a PTAB trial, a certificate under 37 CFR 1.323 or 1.324 will not be issued unless a corresponding motion has been granted by the administrative patent judge. For contested cases under 37 CFR part 42 subpart D, 1.324 will not be issued unless a corresponding motion under 42.22 has been granted. Otherwise, determination whether an error has been made, responsibility for the error, and whether issuance is justified will be made by the Certificates of Correction Branch; reports may be requested; patentee notified if no certificate; if certificate issues it will be prepared and forwarded and entered into the file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect extra procedural steps if the patent is involved in contested proceedings; certificate issuance is subject to internal review and recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form PTO/SB/44 (PTO-1050) and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/attorneys are urged to submit the text of the correction on Certificate of Correction form PTO/SB/44 which can serve as camera copy. In addition to the form, the request must include a signed request identifying support in the application for any Office errors in the patent. If the request is not signed, it will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always submit PTO/SB/44 and a signed request showing support for claimed Office errors; unsigned or non-form submissions risk delay or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial approvals and issuance timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where only part of a request can be approved, or where the Office discovers and includes additional corrections, the patentee is notified on the Notification of Approval-in-part form PTOL-404. The certificate is issued approximately 6 weeks thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for partial approvals and expect roughly a 6-week lead time from approval-in-part to issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form content and formatting instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: On PTO/SB/44: (A) identify exact point of error by reference to column and line number of printed patent for specification or claim changes; (B) conserve space by typing single space beginning two lines down from printed message; (C) start correction to each separate column as a sentence and use semicolons to separate corrections within same column where possible; (D) leave a two-inch space blank at bottom of last sheet for signature of attesting officer; (E) use quotation marks to enclose exact subject matter to be deleted or corrected and double hyphens (--) to enclose subject matter to be added, except formulas; (F) for formulas, set out only portion to be corrected or paste photocopy onto form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict adherence to the form formatting instructions avoids processing delays; special handling for formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent holder responsibilities and handling of patent grant copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent grant should be retained by the patentee; the Office does not attach the certificate of correction to the patentee’s copy of the patent. The patent grant will be returned to the patentee if submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect the Office to return an annotated patent with certificate attached; keep original grant in your files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic issuance and public availability of certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: As of January 30, 2024, all certificates of correction are issued electronically; no paper certificates of correction will be reissued in electronic form. The listing of all certificates is available on the USPTO website and images can be accessed in public/private Patent Center views and Patent Public Search. The date the certificate is made available to the public (e.g., added to file history) is the date of issuance, not the Official Gazette publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on electronic records (Patent Center, Patent Public Search) for certificate issuance and dates; Official Gazette listing is secondary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimers and terminal disclaimers general requirements (37 CFR 1.321)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee owning whole or sectional interest may disclaim any complete claim or claims or dedicate to the public the entire term or any terminal part. To be recorded, the disclaimer must: (1) be signed by the patentee or attorney/agent of record; (2) identify the patent and complete claim(s) or term being disclaimed; (3) state the present extent of patentee’s ownership interest in the patent; and (4) be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure disclaimers are signed, identify claims/term precisely, state ownership interest, and include the correct fee to be recordable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant terminal disclaimer requirements (in applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may disclaim or dedicate to the public the entire term or any terminal part of a patent to be granted. Such terminal disclaimer must: (1) be signed by the applicant or attorney/agent of record; (2) specify the portion of term being disclaimed; (3) state present extent of applicant’s ownership interest in the patent to be granted; and (4) be accompanied by fee in § 1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers filed in prosecution must meet the same formal requirements (signature, specification of term portion, ownership statement, fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer to obviate judicially created double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate judicially created double patenting must: (1) comply with (b)(2)-(b)(4); (2) be signed in accordance with the signature rules; and (3) include a provision that any patent granted on that application or any patent subject to the reexamination proceeding shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patent is commonly owned with the application or patent which formed the basis for the judicially created double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers intended to defeat judicial double patenting must include a common-ownership enforceability limitation and proper execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer for joint-research-agreement disqualified prior art (non-common ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate double patenting based upon a patent or application not commonly owned but disqualified as prior art due to activities within the scope of a joint research agreement must: (1) comply with (b)(2)-(b)(4); (2) be signed per rules; and (3) include a provision waiving the right to separately enforce any patent granted on that application or any patent subject to the reexamination proceeding and the patent which formed the basis for the double patenting, and that any patent granted shall be enforceable only while the patents are not separately enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on joint-research agreement exceptions, include the required waiver of separate enforcement and proper signature and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between statutory disclaimer and terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory disclaimer denotes a disclaimer of one or more claims of an issued patent (35 U.S.C. 253); a terminal disclaimer denotes a disclaimer of the entire term or any terminal part of the term of a patent or a patent to be granted. Although both provided by statute, historically the phrases distinguish disclaimers of claims (statutory) vs disclaimers of term (terminal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct type of disclaimer based on whether relinquishing claims (statutory) or patent term (terminal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA signature and execution variations for disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA rules provided alternative signing options for applicants/assignees/attorneys depending on whether an assignee of part or whole interest existed; the terminal disclaimer must identify the portion of term disclaimed, state extent of ownership interest, and be accompanied by fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legacy/pre-AIA filings, ensure the correct signatory (applicant, assignee, or attorney) executes the disclaimer consistent with chain-of-title facts.
